title: Iterative query refinement loop (foundational)
description: The agent runs a loop: issue a query, score the results, then refine the query from the best hits' distinctive terms. Refinement adds terms that discriminate good hits from bad ones, following the classic relevance-feedback idea from information retrieval. Each iteration's query is logged so the search path stays auditable. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
queries = ['archive search speed']
for i in range(3):
    q = queries[-1]
    queries.append(q + ' index' if i == 0 else q + ' latency')
print('query path:', queries)
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Autonomous Search Agent practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Result triage by promise score (foundational)
description: Retrieved results are triaged into pursue, skim, or discard bands by a promise score combining relevance and novelty. Only the pursue band gets deep follow-up; the skim band gets a glance; discards are logged but not opened. Triage concentrates the step budget where discovery is most likely. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
results = [('r1', 0.9), ('r2', 0.55), ('r3', 0.2)]
for rid, s in results:
    band = 'pursue' if s >= 0.75 else 'skim' if s >= 0.4 else 'discard'
    print(rid, round(s, 2), '->', band)
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Autonomous Search Agent practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Discovery following with depth cap (foundational)
description: When a result looks promising, the agent follows its citations and related records, but each follow decrements a depth allowance. The depth cap prevents the agent from wandering down an endless citation chain away from the original mission. Followed discoveries are tagged with their path so their relevance to the mission stays visible. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
depth, path = 3, ['seed']
while depth > 0:
    path.append('follow-' + str(4 - depth)); depth -= 1
print('follow path:', path, '| depth exhausted -> return to mission')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Autonomous Search Agent practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Step budgeting with graceful stop (foundational)
description: The agent operates under a hard step budget covering queries issued, pages opened, and follows taken. As the budget depletes, the agent shifts from exploration to consolidation, spending its last steps on the most promising leads. When the budget hits zero the agent stops and reports, never mid-thought without a summary. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
demo:
budget = 10
spent = 7
mode = 'explore' if spent < budget * 0.7 else 'consolidate'
print(f'steps left: {budget - spent} | mode: {mode}')
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Autonomous Search Agent practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.

title: Loop guard against repeated queries (foundational)
description: A guard tracks every query issued and blocks repeats and near-repeats above 0.9 similarity, forcing the agent to make progress instead of cycling. If the agent proposes a blocked query three times, the mission is replanned with fresh angles. The guard is what separates an autonomous agent from an infinite loop with ambition. Foundational form: the core technique demonstrated on a minimal example.
provenance: Public computer-science methods literature (Autonomous Search Agent practice); cross-checked against standard references, 2026-10-21.
